resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), Residential Resale Inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Cherry Hill Township Community Development, Property Maintenance Department
resale_co.lead_time: No minimum lead time published. Inspections occur within 7 business days of receipt of application and fee.
requirements: Exterior-only inspection by the Property Maintenance Officer; no one needs to be home
Sidewalks, walkways, stairs and driveways in good repair, including sidewalk up to the curb line
Fences, detached garages and other accessory structures structurally sound
Dead or dying trees and hazardous limbs removed or trimmed
Grading and drainage: no ponding, no runoff onto neighbors
Sump pump and roof drain discharge not affecting neighbors or the roadway
No ground surface hazards such as holes or broken walks
No unregistered, uninsured or disassembled vehicles stored on the property

fees.label: CCO exterior inspection
fees.quote: The cost of inspection is $100, due prior to inspection.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online (the office approves first, then SDL Portal emails a payment request), or download the paper application and mail it or drop it off with a check or money order payable to Cherry Hill Township at 820 Mercer Street, Room 202, Cherry Hill, NJ 08002. The fee must be paid before the inspection. No refunds once paid.

evidence.quote: Cherry Hill homeowners are required to obtain a Certificate of Continued Occupancy prior to the resale of any single-family residential property in Cherry Hill.

Before any single-family home sale can proceed to closing, the home's exterior property areas must be inspected by Cherry Hill's Property Maintenance Officer, to ensure that these areas comply with the township's property maintenance standards.
Some condominiums and townhomes are excluded from this requirement.
please contact the Property Maintenance Department at 856-834-3364
APPLICATION FOR RESIDENTIAL CONTINUED CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY
Inspections take place between 8:30 am and 3:00 pm and will occur within seven (7) business days of receipt of application and fee.
Fee: $100.00 made payable to: Cherry Hill Township

resale_co.notes: The township pages say the CCO applies to single-family homes and do not say whether two-family homes need one. Some condominiums and townhomes (non-fee-simple) are exempt; the township publishes a list at https://chnj.gov/DocumentCenter/View/6561/Non-Fee-Simple-Properties. The paper application PDF repeats the $100.00 fee. The CCO section of the Township code was not found in Chapter 15 (Property Maintenance) or Chapter 13 (Building and Housing) on ecode360, so the township page is the main source. Rental inspections are a separate Community Development program (856-488-7870).

requirements: 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on every level, in every bedroom (on the ceiling), and within 10 feet of all bedroom doors; hardwired alarms cannot be swapped for battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
Smoke and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently on the house and visible from the street (mailbox or light post numbers not accepted)

Homes with a secondary power source (solar, generator, battery storage) need a permanent, non-handwritten label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter, such as 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power'
Homes with a low-voltage fire alarm system must have it tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection and show the certification to the inspector
The township page says fire extinguishers are no longer required

authorities.name: Cherry Hill Fire Department (Cherry Hill Fire District #13)
authorities.lead_time: Submit the request 3 to 4 weeks before the settlement date. Certificates are valid for 90 days.

fees.label: Request received 8 or more calendar days before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received eight (8) calendar days or more prior to the settlement date: $100.00

fees.label: Request received 4 to 7 calendar days before settlement (sheet says 'seven (7) calendar days prior')
fees.quote: Requests received seven (7) calendar days prior to the settlement date: $115.00

fees.label: Request received 3 calendar days or less before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received three (3) calendar days or less prior to the settlement date: $162.00

fees.label: Senior discount, sellers 62 and over (off the initial fee, proof of age required)
fees.quote: Sellers age 62 & over may deduct $30.00 from the initial inspection fee - PROOF OF AGE REQUIRED

authorities.how_to_apply: Submit the online Residential Inspection Request Form (not for re-inspections or rentals). Pay at the time of inspection by credit card, check or money order payable to CHFD; no cash. The certificate is issued at the inspection if the home passes and payment is received. Temporary certificates are not issued.

evidence.quote: When selling a one or two family home in Cherry Hill, you must obtain a Certificate of Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Detector Compliance CSACMAPFEC 5:70-2.3 (a) prior to the settlement.
Fire extinguishers are NO longer required.
Requests must be submitted using the online form located at www.chnj.gov/fire, 3 to 4 weeks prior to the settlement date. Email questions to sdi@chfd.org or call 856-429-7441.
SACMC-2, smoke alarm/carbon monoxide inspections requested on all one- and two-family dwellings between four and seven calendar days' notice of the settlement date: $115.

evidence.doc_date: 2026-07 (LEA registry as of June 30, 2026; key: D = Fire District)

fire_cert.notes: Fee sheet is marked effective 1/1/2026 to 12/31/2026. New this check: the Township code (Section 16-1.8d, read on ecode360) has the same amounts and settles the middle tier: $115 applies to requests made between four and seven calendar days before settlement. The code also says the fee covers one inspection (including an attempted inspection where entry was not gained), each re-inspection is $35, and a certificate is valid for 90 days from issuance. The fire department is governed by a Board of Fire Commissioners (Cherry Hill Fire District #13, 1100 Marlkress Road). The township page says extinguishers are no longer required, matching the 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19). Fire Official Joseph V Cornforth (jcornforth@chfd.org, 856-795-1340) is from the state fire directory; the resale line is 856-429-7441, sdi@chfd.org.

other_items.label: Two separate inspections
other_items.detail: The Property Maintenance CCO is in addition to the Cherry Hill Fire Department smoke alarm inspection.

open_questions: Do two-family homes need the Property Maintenance CCO? The township pages only mention single-family homes.
How long is the CCO valid? Not stated.
Which Township code section sets the $100 CCO fee? Not found on ecode360.
